The Hebrew ends with as this day without a separate passive clause; BSB supplies as is being done this day.
The Hebrew says in the ears of our God and calls the inheritors your sons after you; BSB expresses hearing and uses your descendants.
The Hebrew speaks of a whole heart and a willing soul; BSB uses wholeheartedly and a willing mind.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names the portico without an explicit temple noun; BSB supplies of the temple.
The Hebrew describes everything that was with him in the spirit; BSB names David and says he had it in mind.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats gold and service, service; BSB condenses this to gold articles for every kind of service.
The Hebrew repeats lampstand and lampstand to distribute the weights and uses singular its lamps; BSB expresses this as each lampstand and its lamps.
The Hebrew repeats table and table; BSB uses each table.
The Hebrew repeats bowl and bowl for both metals; BSB uses each gold dish and each silver bowl.
The Hebrew describes the cherubim spreading out and covering the ark without an explicit wings noun; BSB supplies their wings.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed; BSB supplies said David.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the willing, skilled workers are with you and the people are for all your words; BSB expresses this as being at Solomon’s disposal and command.
